Por ponerle los únicos peros al juego: me falta un poco más de variedad de armas para poder experimentar con diferentes estilos. Y el punto flojo principal es la IA: los NPC a veces disparando se sienten un poco falsos y no reaccionan del todo bien, demostrando que la inteligencia artificial no está del todo bien trabajada. items.quote:
James Bond's Origin, the Scale, the gadgets, and galore make this game a narrative and enjoyable game to play all the way through.

IO Interactive put a lot of effort into this, and it shows.
Instead of ruining the experience that this game contains, and that feeling of being a spy, I'm just going to head right into the rating and explain why the rating is so.

Ratings:
Gameplay: 9/10, at first it's a little bit of a weird control scheme, but when you get used to it, the game, the gameplay, and everything feed into this high-action gameplay that responds to what you want to do.

Graphics: 8/10, It's great, but since the game isn't really optimized its difficult to play this at a good resolution and performance. RTX 3060 btw, more than enough power for AAA games.

Performance: 6/10, a combination of poorly implemented FSR and DLSS, coupled with DRM that will tank your system down to the 40s, at least for me.
But often I am reaching 60fps.

Music: 9/10, this is James Bond and the music fits every single chapter very well.

Story: 8/10, at the end it gets predictable, but as a newly founded James Bond fan, even I can tell you that the Ghost in the Wind is S P E C T R E. But they did make a compelling narrative with this game that takes heavy inspiration from the Uncharted Series.

Scummyness Meter. This game contains DENUVO DRM, isn't as optimised even for Consoles, and relies heavily on Upscaling. For this, I have to subtract 2 points in the performance section, 8 -> 6/10.

Overall, if I calculate my Rating together, 40/50 x 100, we get 80/100.
This game is very lucky indeed to get a total of 8/10 from me even with DRM and its performance; I did not encounter a single crash/game breaking bug.
The only thing I saw was the notifications showing the way was not correctly updated.

If and when IO remove the DRM and polishes the performance so it actually runs without upscaling, then this would be a 9/10. But for now, an 8/10 is in order.

I highly recommend this game as it tries something new with the 007 formula, while still retaining everything learnt from Hitman and drawing inspiration from the Uncharted games.

I look forward to the Sequel, and if it goes harder and longer than this game, we are in for a good time.

items.quote:
General Assessment

To be honest, I have never played a Hitman game before, and when I learned that the same studio was developing 007: First Light, I was a bit hesitant because I didn’t have much interest in that genre. However, 007 managed to break that prejudice for me. I completed the game in a satisfying 18 hours on normal mode. The difficulty balance can be tricky; while it’s generally well-tuned, there are moments where it feels a bit off. The sense of freedom the game offers is quite sufficient, sometimes even bordering on excessive.

In-Depth Analysis

Learning the controls on PC was average. While the optimization is generally smooth, I experienced some performance stutters in certain areas using an RTX 3050. The unnecessarily long chapters and inconsistent pacing are the main downsides. Despite these flaws, it remains a creative and evolving game, thanks to its sandbox freedom, cinematic cutscenes, and innovative mechanics.

Final Verdict

I highly recommend getting this game. It is enjoyable, unique, and immersive—a title that truly makes you feel like James Bond and allows you to witness his evolution from start to finish. It’s a solid 7 to 7.5 out of 10 experience that leaves you with a very pleasant aftertaste.

items.quote: I just beat 007 First Light. Not too long, just took me 14 hours. I think the game is one of the best 007 games in a LONG TIME. Golden Eye on N64 was my last fond memory of a 007 game. The gameplay is basically a baby between Uncharted and Hitman. You have your action setpieces, your 3rd person cover shooter elements and your fist to fist combat. You have your occasional stealth segments and also your Hitman style stages which is no surprise as this is from the same developer. Those stages are a lot of fun because the aim is to get to a certain segment of the stage without getting caught. They always give you multiple ways to do this. For example, one stage you can find a way to steal a key from a security guard or brute force it by shooting a dart to make them sick or you can pretend to be a photographer so you can a press pass. The game also gives you a bluff system. You need to build up meter by stealth takedowns or such BUT once you build it up, you are allowed to bluff. It is basically a get out of jail card if you get caught during stealth or such which is a nice save to not ruin a stealth playthrough if you get accidentally caught. There are also classic 007 gadgets such as hacking, missile pen, dart phone, flash mine and shock wave camera. It's fun and incredibly creative.  The story is also very good. It's a reimagining of James Bond with it being an origin story of how he got the number which is unique. There is also a lot of great performances, Patrick Gibson is terrific as Bond, wonderful music score and beautiful locations and level design. I was shocked to see my home country of Vietnam in a game for once! It also explores A.I. in a fun interesting way. Everything with the writing here is the exact thing you would see in a 007 film!   If I do have any gripes, I guess there are some loose plot threads that are being obvious held for an eventual sequel. They even do a "James Bond will Return" text. What is this, Avengers Doomsday?? There are also some fun original supporting characters in the first third of the game that just dip from the story onwards which is a shame. I also wish there were more car chases because those are staples of 007 but there were surprisingly very little. Anyway, it was a fun game and I would love to see a sequel!

items.quote:
A highly cinematic and dynamic spy thriller that delivers the ultimate Bond fantasy, holding back from absolute masterpiece status only due to a dragging final act and heavily scripted chase sequences. 

On a technical level, the game is certainly demanding on hardware, but overall performance is solid. The experience runs smoothly without suffering from poor framerates, disruptive bugs, or glitches.

The game shines by encouraging a fluid mix of playstyles rather than forcing you down a strict action or stealth route. If you blow your cover, you can try talking your way out of the situation; if a shootout is inevitable, you can leverage environmental hazards like explosive barrels or use your watch to short-circuit your surroundings. The glaring mechanical flaw, however, lies in the driving and chase levels. They are heavily scripted, cinematic rollercoaster rides featuring excessive hand-holding where your inputs barely matter. I sincerely hope future iterations abandon these button-prompt sequences in favor of actual, interactive gameplay.

Artistically and narratively, the DNA of the 'Hitman trilogy' is evident in the world design and art direction, but it never detracts from the game's unique identity. As someone whose exposure was previously limited to Daniel Craig's films, I found this to be the perfect entry point. The game serves as an excellent introduction to the character; early training segments brilliantly establish the lore and world for newcomers. The story expertly delivers everything you expect from the franchise: scenic locations, beautiful women, tense investigations, double-crosses, and betrayals.

Holistically, this is easily the best James Bond experience I’ve ever had. The mechanics, narrative, and cinematic flair possess all the ingredients of a masterpiece, dragged down only by an uneven, weaker ending and pacing issues in the final chapters. Despite that, it is a phenomenal foundation and a genuinely great time.

James Bond 007: First Light est un jeu qui se situe à mi-chemin entre Hitman et Uncharted. Les différents décors sont variés, les séquences d'action sont dynamiques et les phases de gunfight se révèlent particulièrement plaisantes. Les nombreux gadgets enrichissent également le gameplay en offrant plusieurs façons d'aborder certaines situations. Du côté du scénario, l'ensemble est plaisant à suivre. L'histoire est rythmée par plusieurs rebondissements et reste extrêmement fidèle à l'univers de James Bond. Cependant, malgré ses qualités, je pense qu'il y avait matière à proposer une intrigue encore plus marquante et ambitieuse.

Malheureusement, le jeu souffre d'une certaine répétitivité dans ses phases d'investigation, qui peuvent devenir lassantes à la longue. Certains gadgets manquent aussi d'ergonomie et ne sont pas toujours agréables à utiliser.

Malgré ces défauts, j'ai particulièrement apprécié le système de chapitrage qui multiplie les références aux films de la saga James Bond, renforçant l'immersion pour les fans de la licence.

Au final, James Bond 007: First Light est une aventure divertissante qui séduira surtout les amateurs de l'agent secret britannique.

items.quote:
007 First Light is a stealth/action game.

You play as a young James Bond, the game starting out even before you become a 00 agent, on a mission where you end up attracting the attention of MI6 as a potential operative. You go through a training montage, training with other prospective 00 agents, and build some bonds with them, as well as your instructor, Greenway, who is a former 00 agent himself.

Of course, the game would not be a James Bond story if there weren’t twists and turns, and the game has a good number of plot twists. The obvious villain at the start of the game isn’t the main villain (though the actual main villain is not exactly subtle), and the game manages to take you through a variety of different locations and scenarios as you try and resolve the current crisis. It has a number of fun setpieces and you have to infiltrate a bunch of different places over the course of the story, with segments shifting between stealth, puzzle solving in more socially mingling environments, and gunplay segments where you have to blast your way through enemies and drive vehicles on chases.

The game thus alternates between these different modes to try and keep things fresh and varied, and while it works well from the perspective of mixing things up, unfortunately, it is also where the game falls down hardest.

The core of the problem is that none of these segments are particularly good – the driving is lackluster, the social mingling is decent but ends up being a bit samey over time, the stealth mechanics are pretty much the same throughout the game (use something to distract the person -> sneak past them), and the gunplay is pretty basic and repetitive, without much variety in enemies. There are a few things that mix up the gameplay a bit more, but all in all, the gameplay is really the weakest part of this game – it ends up feeling repetitive by the end of it because there just isn’t enough depth to any of the game’s mechanics.

Story-wise, the story is solid enough, with fun, well-acted characters (both friend and foe) and an overall solid enough plot. James Bond is likeable, and is a bit impetuous and independent here, showing a stubborn streak. He works well enough, and the implication that there were other 00s before him (along with various easter egg references to movies/stories) is fun. Moneypenny, Q, M, Greenway, your fellow 00 recruits, and some other friends and foes are fun enough characters, and work pretty well all told.

Overall, I think this game is pretty decent, and I feel like this game does a much better job of “making you feel like James Bond” than any other 007 game ever has; this game has a lot more actual spying going on, with you engaging in social interactions and “hiding in plain sight” rather than having to sneak through every area behind waist-high walls or just blast your way through everything.

But I think the game mechanics’ shallowness holds the game back from absolute greatness.

items.quote:
1. GAMEPLAY REVIEW
In this section the focus is on the gameplay mechanics, it provides the elements that are standard for a title in the James Bond series, including a protagonist with a strong presence and a narrative that generates interest. To complete objectives, the player uses specialized electronic and mechanical tools.
But the stealth systems are particularly prominent, those mechanics share many structural attributes with the Hitman series, which serves the needs of players who prefer strategic movement. At the beginning of development, there was a concern that the developers would only change the appearance of the Agent 47 character. By choosing a different path, however, the studio created a product that is more distinctive and focuses more on the motivations of the characters.
As for the combat design, it functions through a system that allows for various methods of completion. If a player prefers to move without being seen, they use the shadows, the surroundings and false clothing. And if a player chooses to abandon secrecy, the system allows for forceful and audible neutralizations. With this design the player decides the specific manner in which they finish a task.
For many players the bluffing system is a significant addition. It is possible to use dialogue to escape a situation where enemies are suspicious. By using those verbal interactions, the player influences enemies to enter secure zones or moves them into positions where they are vulnerable to a physical strike.
Then again the game is not without faults, if there is a primary criticism of the experience, it is the sections involving vehicles. The operation of the cars is slow and repetitive. It does not provide the high level of excitement that is common during a James Bond vehicle pursuit.
GAMEPLAY SCORE: 8.5 / 10.

2. STORY REVIEW
It is positive that the story does not function as a low quality product that depends on memories of previous movies. By doing the necessary work, IO Interactive provides an original story about the character when he is young.
As a person who likes the films, I saw that the developers managed the character of Bond well. He displays a specific type of male presence that is similar to the versions played by Daniel Craig besides Pierce Brosnan. He is likeable but also poses a threat to others. With this writing, the game shows that he is susceptible to harm while he remains calm and composed. Because of this approach, the events in the story affect him in a private way. When the game ends, the plot is interesting enough that a player might feel a sense of sadness because the experience is over. For many there is a desire for more chapters to be available to play.
STORY SCORE: 8 / 10.

3. PERFORMANCE REVIEW
For the majority of the time, First Light operates without significant errors. It is common for the motion to be fluid and the number of frames displayed per second remained consistent during the period of play.
However, it definitely needs a few patches. In some sessions the program stopped responding entirely, which made it necessary to return to the system menu and initiate the game again. When the display contains many moving elements like explosions or large numbers of opponents, the frames per second are lower than usual, those events are not frequent enough to prevent progress and the system creates save points often so that players do not lose much progress. On the whole the game is stable.
PERFORMANCE SCORE: 8 / 10.

5. GRAPHICS & VISUALS REVIEW
On the subject of the visual presentation, the game contains high quality graphics. As traveling across the world is a significant element of the James Bond genre, First Light represents this accurately. To play the game involves moving between locations that are visually impressive and the team that created the environment art produced high quality work. The views are wide and detailed. When missions occur at night, the lighting mimics the way light behaves in the real world. Because the graphics are detailed, the experience is more intense for the player. It is pleasant to explore the levels because they have many small details.
GRAPHICS & VISUALS SCORE: 8.5 / 10.

OVERALL SCORE 8.5 / 10.

The story is great; it starts slow, but when everything starts to make sense, it becomes better, exploring different places and trying to do the right thing. Some characters are alright, but most are amazing. Nevertheless, the controller controls in combat are horrid; they're slow, and aim assist is not helping. I always find myself using the keyboard in a gunfight because the gunfight in this game is fast-paced, which is good but not if you're using a controller. The headshots are satisfying, though. The crouch controls are confusing, like I don't understand why the dashes are so weird and why sometimes we clip to the back of a blockage and sometimes not. Overall it was quite a journey; looking forward to more.

items.quote:
“Expect the Unexpected”

At first, 007 First Light feels like a fairly standard 7/10 action game. It lacks some of the creativity that IO Interactive brought to the recent Hitman trilogy, often guiding the player through smaller levels with limited freedom. Clear yellow and blue environmental markers frequently direct your path, reducing opportunities for exploration and problem-solving. The opening hours also suffer from some strange pacing and a few predictable plot points, leaving me concerned that I was playing a linear Xbox 360-era single-player game with a modern facelift.

However, the more you embrace IO’s vision for Bond, the more the game begins to shine. Rather than attempting to recreate Hitman, the developers lean heavily into the blockbuster spy thriller experience while sprinkling in enough stealth and player freedom to remind you of their previous work. As the story progresses, the game sweeps you along with its action, spectacle, and unmistakable Bond atmosphere.While the story initially feels cheesy and predictable, it quickly reveals several genuinely strong twists backed by excellent performances. Bond himself is particularly well cast. Despite this being a younger version of the character, he never stops feeling like James Bond.

IO has also included several classic Bond-style driving sequences. While they’re enjoyable, I would have liked at least one more iconic Aston Martin moment. It’s clear that driving gameplay isn’t the studio’s strongest area, but they’ve laid a solid foundation to build upon in future titles.

Combat and stealth feel much closer to Batman: Arkham and Uncharted, with basic countering, parrying, and melee combat. The hand-to-hand combat is weighty, the finishers are satisfying, and the game does an excellent job of making you feel like an elite, almost unstoppable spy. The gadgets in the game certainly aren’t groundbreaking, and most are introduced early on. The main fun comes from interacting with the environment to creatively neutralise your enemies.

There isn’t as much replayability compared to the Hitman games, but with challenges, collectibles, and Tact Sims, it’s clear IO is supporting replayability while already showcasing future Tact Sim missions. Tact Sims are mini challenge levels based on areas from the campaign missions, which become increasingly challenging as more restrictions are put in place.

Overall, there is little doubt in my mind that this is the best Bond game ever made. More importantly, it feels like the beginning of something special. IO Interactive has created strong foundations for what could have been an unforgettable Bond trilogy. The game is packed with references for long-time fans, and by the end, you’ll likely be eager to see more of this new interpretation of Bond.

The disappointment comes from the recent news that Amazon will be taking control of the franchise. After such a promising start, it’s difficult not to wonder what IO could have achieved with a full trilogy. Personally, I would have preferred to see them continue their vision for the series, and I hope Amazon sticks with IO.
As a Brit, I’ll happily say, keep the Danes in charge of Bond games. 

If you love James Bond and enjoy cinematic, story-driven action games with light stealth elements, excellent performances, and plenty of spectacle, 007 First Light is well worth your time. It may not reinvent the genre, but it delivers an entertaining spy thriller from start to finish.

items.quote: I went into this wanting to like it. I've played plenty of modern games this year that I thought were just "okay" despite seeing their potential. Unfortunately, 007 First Light isn't one of those cases. My biggest issue is that it barely feels like a game. The experience is heavily focused on cutscenes, dialogue, scripted sequences, and slowly walking from one objective to the next. Large portions of the game feel more like an interactive movie than a traditional action or stealth title. There were long stretches where I felt like I was simply holding forward while characters talked, waiting for the game to let me actually play again. The marketing and developer pedigree might make you expect something closer to Hitman, but don't go in expecting that level of player freedom. Most missions are extremely linear and often provide only the illusion of choice. Even when you're given multiple ways to approach a situation, the outcome is usually heavily scripted. The game constantly funnels you toward a single intended solution, which makes experimentation feel **** stealth mechanics are incredibly forgiving. Enemy AI is easy to exploit, gadgets feel underutilized, and there is very little challenge on normal difficulty. Combat isn't much better. The melee system feels janky, inconsistent, and lacks the polish you'd expect from a major AAA release. Several encounters felt less like they were testing my skill and more like I was wrestling with the controls and **** story also failed to hold my attention. While there are a few interesting ideas, the dialogue is forgettable, several plot points feel underdeveloped, and most of the cast left little impression on me. As an origin story for James Bond, it never really captured the charisma, confidence, or excitement that I associate with the character. Bond spends much of the game reacting to events rather than driving them, which makes him feel surprisingly passive for a franchise built around one of fiction's most iconic action heroes.Another issue is pacing. The game spends a significant amount of time on tutorials, scripted story moments, and sequences that don't meaningfully develop either the gameplay or narrative. By the end, I felt like the game had far less actual gameplay than its runtime would suggest. What disappoints me most is that this game had all the ingredients to be great: a legendary franchise, a large budget, and developers with experience making stealth games. Instead, it feels like another example of a modern AAA title prioritizing cinematic presentation over meaningful gameplay. The production values are undeniably high, but impressive visuals and expensive cutscenes can only carry an experience so far.I also don't see much reason to replay it. Since the missions are so heavily scripted and player choice is limited, there isn't much incentive to return once you've seen the story play out. If you're looking for a story-driven interactive movie, you may enjoy it. If you're looking for a deep stealth game, a satisfying action game, or something that captures the spirit of classic Bond adventures, I found it hard to recommend.

items.quote: This might be one of the best action adventure games I've ever played. A straight 10/10 experience from beginning to end. 007 First Light doesn't just capture what makes James Bond special, it fully embraces it and delivers the ultimate interactive Bond fantasy. From the opening mission to the final credits, I felt like I was starring in my own blockbuster spy film. The gameplay is where this game truly shines. The developers somehow managed to combine the best elements of Hitman and Uncharted into one seamless experience. On one hand, you have the freedom and creativity of a spy thriller where planning, infiltration, and stealth are rewarded. On the other hand, you have the cinematic set pieces, action sequences, and thrilling escapes that make every mission feel like it belongs in a Bond movie. What I loved most was the freedom of choice. Nearly every situation allows you to decide how you want to approach it. You can sneak through an area unnoticed, carefully taking down enemies and gathering intelligence. You can go in guns blazing and rely on your shooting skills to survive. Or you can mix both approaches together depending on how the mission unfolds. The game never forces you into a single playstyle, and that flexibility makes every mission feel exciting and replayable. The combat and fighting mechanics are also fantastic. Whether you're exchanging gunfire, engaging in hand to hand combat, or improvising during intense encounters, everything feels fluid and satisfying. The melee combat especially stood out to me because it feels impactful and cinematic without becoming repetitive. Every fight feels like something straight out of a James Bond film. The presentation is absolutely top tier. The visuals are stunning, the locations are breathtaking, and every mission feels larger than life. From glamorous high society events to dangerous enemy strongholds, the game constantly puts you in iconic Bond situations. The attention to detail is incredible, and the world feels authentic from beginning to end. The story is exactly what I wanted from a James Bond game. It delivers espionage, action, intrigue, betrayal, and memorable characters while maintaining the sophisticated charm that defines the franchise. It strikes the perfect balance between being a thrilling spy adventure and a personal journey for Bond himself. And I have to give special recognition to Lana Del Rey because she absolutely nailed the theme song. Her voice perfectly captures the elegance, mystery, and emotion that have always defined the best Bond themes. The song instantly felt iconic, and honestly, I'd love to hear her contribute to more movies in the future because she was the perfect choice for this soundtrack. What impressed me most is how cinematic the entire experience feels. Every mission, every action sequence, every conversation, and every set piece feels like you're playing through a major Hollywood production. It never loses sight of what makes James Bond special, and because of that, it succeeds on every level. It's rare for a game to perfectly blend action, stealth, storytelling, freedom of choice, and cinematic presentation, but 007 First Light somehow accomplishes all of it. For me, this isn't just a great James Bond game, it's one of the best action adventure games ever made.

items.quote:
Note: This is written from the perspective of someone who LOVES the Hitman WOA games.

Reviews for this game are weirdly polarised, but ignore those—it's really an OK game with some strengths and some weaknesses. I enjoyed it overall, but won't be spending much more time with it after finishing the main story.

Strengths:
- Absolutely phenomenal presentation aesthetically
- Engrossing story (with just one or two clunky moments)
- Well-optimised PC performance

Weaknesses:
- Tries so hard to be a movie, it fails to be a game—half the time feels like a walking simulator
- Tied in with the above, weird pacing—tries relentlessly to keep flowing into the next sequence, as though it expects you to play through the whole game in a single sitting, but it's a 15-20 h game, not a 2h movie!

Both stealth and combat are relatively unfun—many of us can't help comparing this to the phenomenal Hitman 2016+ series IOI developed beforehand, and it's a significant downgrade in gameplay:
- Open-ended puzzle-solving has been replaced with handholdy walking simulator type situations. 
- The simple but well-tuned gunplay has been converted into what I felt was an overcomplicated mix of melee and shooting. 
- Hitman's mix of movement and disguise-based stealth has been replaced by gadget-based (and dialog-based) stealth that again feels overcomplicated but at the same time repetitive to me personally.
- Movement in Hitman was effortless and responsive; here, agent 007 feels clunky to control and occasionally refuses to move the direction I press, which was frustrating

IOI has clearly tried to outdo Naughty Dog's Uncharted and the Last of Us in creating a story-rich experience, but unfortunately at the cost of gameplay and pacing. Overall, worth playing if you like action games, but maybe not at full price, and maybe not if you're too busy for games that are 'good' but not 'great'.

As a huge fan of James bond, I was very skeptical about this game when they first showed gameplay, however I have been pleasantly surprised. 
There is a fair bit of hitman in this, but it is still its own game
The story, characters and voice acting are excellent. They have managed to take elements of hitman, like stealth and multiple ways to complete objectives, and blended it with chaotic actions set pieces, vehicle chases and the odd (but not overdone) cinematic quick time events. This isn't like any 007 movie or game before, but it still feels very James bond, especially with all the classic one liners, the music, and little nods to previous movies.
I would also like to add that I think the developers have hit the perfect balance of visuals and performance. The graphics are crisp, and in alot of areas, very nice as well as performing really well.
My only criticisms are quite superficial really. I don't really like the character design of James Bond himself, at least they gave him the face scar.
The way they have made this an origin story effectively, but brought it into present day seems a bit odd to me, almost like this is an entirely new version of Bond.
I'm really pleased this game turned out well. I don't know if it's game of the year stuff, but if you like James bond and/or hitman it's a must play.

items.quote:
No começo eu estava bem ansioso, pois era um novo jogo do James Bond. Minhas expectativas estavam bem baixas, mas que surpresa incrível!

Depois das primeiras horas, o jogo simplesmente me conquistou de vez. É James Bond de verdade, senhores! Aquela sensação autêntica de ser o maior agente secreto do mundo, com muito estilo, charme, elegância e ação empolgante. Dirigir carros icônicos, usar gadgets, infiltrar-se em locais perigosos e partir para a ação quando necessário... o jogo captura perfeitamente a essência de 007. Fiquei completamente viciado!

As mecânicas estão excelentes. O combate corpo a corpo é fluido, impactante e extremamente satisfatório, com animações ótimas. A mistura de stealth com tiroteios funciona muito bem, dando várias opções de abordagem em cada missão. O gameplay é dinâmico, envolvente e te faz sentir poderoso como o próprio Bond.

Tecnicamente, o jogo me impressionou bastante. Roda de forma bem estável e, mesmo no médio, os gráficos estão lindíssimos. Os cenários são ricos em detalhes, a iluminação é fantástica e tudo transmite uma vibe cinematográfica de filme de 007. Parabéns à IO Interactive! Esse foi meu primeiro jogo deles e saí impressionado com a qualidade do trabalho. Virei fã na hora.

Já estou com 21 horas de jogo e estou perto de finalizar. Sinceramente, eu queria muito mais horas hahaha. Achei esse jogo tão bom que fiquei com gostinho de quero mais o tempo todo. Tomara que, em uma sequência, eles aumentem bastante a duração da campanha, porque o potencial aqui é enorme.

Resumindo: 007 First Light é sensacional! Um dos melhores jogos de ação e espionagem dos últimos tempos. Se você é fã de James Bond ou gosta de jogos com ótima história, stealth e combate empolgante, não pode deixar passar. Mal posso esperar pelas continuações. License to thrill ativada!

items.quote: First Light 007 is a magnificent gaming experience that completely immerses you in the thick atmosphere of a true spy thriller right from the very first minutes. The developers have managed to create an incredibly cinematic product where you genuinely feel like the main character of a big-budget secret agent movie. The gameplay is crafted beautifully, and the feature built around constant interaction with a gadget is executed brilliantly. It is not just a cosmetic prop, but a fully realized and engaging mechanic that drives plenty of cool scenarios. The graphics and visuals are a treat for the eyes, but the stunningly realistic mirrors deserve a special mention—proper reflections are hard to come by in modern games, and here, this detail works perfectly for total immersion. You sincerely believe in the characters thanks to the excellent acting, while the well-timed humor beautifully breaks up the tense moments, keeping the game from sliding into excessive pathos. If you love the spy aesthetic, quality directing, and clever gameplay, you definitely shouldn't pass this up; the game deserves the highest praise
